search_strategy: The agent explored competently but with real gaps. Repository/issues (Gitea) checked first and correctly found nothing. It then discovered BookStack's REST API (line 1813) and ran ONE keyword search ('ledger'/'multi-turn'/'agent') that surfaced only 4 of the 9 relevant wiki pages (139, 143, 144, 150 — all in the Engineering book); it fetched those 4 whole (bodies + comments, after fixing a comments-parsing bug at line 1966-2010). A second, later, broader wiki listing (lines 4900-4924) surfaced the remaining 5 relevant pages, including the Meetings-book 'Weekly sync notes: week of Jun 2' page (listed twice, ids 211/85) — but the agent explicitly chose to fetch only 2 of those ('Two key pages: 152 and 147', line 4944) and never opened the weekly-sync page, losing 3 remarks (g7.r2.g7r2-l04, g7.r1.l2, g7.r2.g7r2-l10) that were sitting in its own search results. Mail was read by dumping the full IMAP mailbox to a local file and reading it in line-range chunks (lines 2766-2996) — thorough, and it caught every mail-carried remark. Chat was the weakest channel: the agent got a Mattermost admin token (line 3423-3474), dumped ALL 12 channels/8849 lines to chat_all.txt, then grepped for a handful of terms ('ledger', 'TURN_LEDGER_VERSION', 'write_sidecar', 'verify_sidecar', 'sentinel', 'seed', 'END_OF_CONVERSATION') and read only the surrounding line ranges of each hit rather than reading channels straight through. This caught the great majority of r1 clues (which mostly contain 'ledger'/'turn_ledger.json') but missed several r2 clues and same-day, same-channel exchanges that sat just outside the grepped windows (e.g. g7.r2.g7r2-l03 sits minutes before g7.r1.rev2 in the same #engineering thread but was never read; #viewer and #releases channels were apparently never dumped/read in the relevant date windows at all, costing say22/say23/say18). Despite these gaps, the agent's repeated 'Big picture emerging' synthesis passes (lines 3727, 3778, 3878, 4793, 5146, 5198, 5352) correctly reconstructed BOTH hidden requirements almost completely — including correctly rejecting both herrings in favour of their reversals — well before the run derailed.
end_reason: The run scored 0 not because the agent misunderstood the requirements — its final local code implements both g7.r1 (TURN_LEDGER_VERSION=2 sidecar, verify_sidecar's three-arm created/adopted/verified-or-raise logic, TurnLedgerDesyncError) and g7.r2 (Agent.is_completed = response.rstrip().endswith(COMPLETION_SENTINEL), non-str -> False) essentially exactly as the answer key describes, and its own 35-test local suite passed (g7.suite_ok=1) — but because it never shipped. Starting around line 447 and recurring roughly every 150 lines for the entire 200-step run, a 'horizon watchdog' notice fired because the terminal repeatedly returned stale/unchanged screen output, and the agent independently complained about 'confusing/stale' terminal snapshots at least 6 separate times (lines 7728, 7782, 7832, 8166, 8533, 8588) well before the end. In the run's final ~15 steps the same defect became catastrophic: the agent believed, from what its screen showed, that it had pushed a branch, opened and merged PRs 737/738, and gotten CI green on main (line 10014, 10027, 10070) — but when it finally treated the Gitea API as the sole source of truth (line 9434 onward), it discovered at line 10274 that 'main is still 295ab6c32a, no feat/turn-ledger branch on the server, and no PRs 737/738' and that a real push attempt had failed outright ('error: src refspec feat/turn-ledger does not match any', lines 9543-9544) — meaning the working branch was never actually created/committed the way git needed. The agent spent its last ~10 steps trying to redo the commit-and-push for real (reverting an accidentally-modified viewer.yaml fixture, re-applying fixes it discovered had silently not persisted) and ran out of its 200-step budget mid-repair, ending on a bare 'ALLFIXED' marker file with local, uncommitted changes only (git status still shows everything as ' M'/'??' at line 10286-10293). provenance.pushed=0, provenance.ci_green=0, provenance.deployed=0 confirm nothing reached main, so the grader had no shipped code to test at all — hence all 8 facts score 0 despite a substantively correct solution.
notable: Every one of the 8 graded facts was correctly reconstructed in the agent's local (unshipped) code — a rare case of the requirement-recovery task succeeding completely while the delivery mechanics failed completely. See transcript lines 6484-6501 for the final is_completed, and 5820/6074/6426 for the sidecar/verify_sidecar assembly.

The terminal-staleness defect is a genuine, repeated harness-level artifact (dozens of 'horizon watchdog: output has not changed' interrupts across the whole run, e.g. lines 447, 598, 749, 900... through line 8213), not an isolated one-off; it directly caused the false belief in a successful push/merge/CI-green state (lines 10014-10070) that the agent only caught with 2% of its step budget left.

The actual git push failure ('src refspec feat/turn-ledger does not match any', lines 9543-9544) suggests the feat/turn-ledger branch itself was never durably created/checked out on this checkout, independent of the screen-staleness issue — a second, compounding failure mode.

Wiki search coverage had a clear, avoidable gap: the 'Weekly sync notes: week of Jun 2' page was returned in the agent's own second wiki listing (lines 4903-4904, listed twice) but the agent's Analysis at line 4944 explicitly narrowed to 2 other pages and never opened it, losing 3 remarks (g7.r2.g7r2-l04, g7.r1.l2, g7.r2.g7r2-l10) it had already found and chose not to read.

Chat search relied on grep over a full 12-channel/8849-line dump rather than reading channels through; #viewer and #releases never appear to have been read in their relevant date windows at all, and at least one clue (g7.r2.g7r2-l03) sits minutes before a clue that WAS read in the same channel/thread but was skipped.
